record.paper_title: Trimer Covers in the Triangular Grid: Twenty Mostly Open Problems
record.original_question: Let T112(a,b) count tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that T112(n+2, 2n+1) equals the nth large Schroder number for every n >= 1?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.
Problem 12: Is it true that T112 (n + 2, 2n + 1) is the "nth large Schroder number" for all n >= 1? Equality has been verified for 1 <= n <= 15.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the triangular lattice with vertices placed at the centers of the unit triangles of the standard tessellation, so that the lattice is bipartite with "up" and "down" triangles. For positive integers $a,b$, the $(a,b)$-benzel is a particular hexagonal region of the triangular grid (a hexagon whose six side-lengths are determined by $a$ and $b$, obtained by truncating corners of an equilateral triangle in a prescribed way). A trimer tile is one of five shapes covering three adjacent unit triangles: the "right stone" and "left stone" (the two orientations of a triangle of three small triangles meeting at a vertex), and three "bones" (three unit triangles in a row, in each of the three lattice directions).

For $i,j\in\{0,1\}$ and $k\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $T_{ijk}(a,b)$ denote the number of tilings of the $(a,b)$-benzel by trimers in which the right stone is allowed iff $i=1$, the left stone is allowed iff $j=1$, and exactly $k$ of the three bone orientations are allowed (with a specified choice of which $k$ orientations).

The large Schröder numbers are $S_n$ with $S_1=2,\ S_2=6,\ S_3=22,\ S_4=90,\ldots$, satisfying $(n+1)S_n = 3(2n-1)S_{n-1} - (n-2)S_{n-2}$ (equivalently OEIS A006318 shifted).

Prove or disprove: for every integer $n\ge 1$,
$$T_{112}(n+2,\, 2n+1) = S_n,$$
where both stone orientations are permitted and exactly two of the three bone orientations are permitted (in the prescribed convention).
